rules.note: Photocopy of your passport, if you have one.
A current photograph is attached to the printed, personally signed application form.

Legalised copy of your bachelor's diploma with its Diploma Supplement, apostilled or super-legalised, with a certified translation into Czech (English translation if Czech is not possible in your country).

Legalised copy of your master's diploma with its Diploma Supplement, apostilled or super-legalised, with a certified translation into Czech (English translation if Czech is not possible in your country).
List of completed subjects and examinations with scope and grades, with a certified translation. Needed if your degree is not yet complete; otherwise your diploma comes with its Diploma Supplement.
CV focused on your studies and employment.
Motivation letter of one A4 page, stressing how you will apply what you learn and how your home country will benefit after you graduate.
Motivation letter of two A4 pages describing the issues you want to focus on in your doctoral studies and how your home country will benefit after you graduate.
Your ideas about the focus of the dissertation, 3 to 5 pages.
Overview of your publication activity. Other documents showing your qualifications and scientific activity can be added if applicable.
Two letters of recommendation from professors teaching at an academic institution.
Legalised copy of your birth certificate with a certified translation into Czech.
Medical confirmation of your health, not more than two months old, on the official form (Annex 4), with a certified translation into English or Czech unless issued in one of them.

Three declarations signed by your own hand: acceptance of the scholarship terms (Annex 1), acceptance of the health services terms (Annex 2), and affirmation of return to your home country after studies (Annex 3).
